key_insight: Adaptive single-copy Clifford measurements can learn any n-qubit stabilizer state with optimal Θ(n) sample complexity, matching Bell-pair methods without requiring multi-copy measurements.
engineering_relevance: This closes a major practical gap for quantum state verification and learning by reducing hardware demands to single-copy operations while preserving sample efficiency, which is important for error correction, benchmarking, and near-term devices.
method: Use an adaptive measurement strategy on individual copies rather than two-copy Bell measurements.
Construct a polynomial-time learner that recovers arbitrary stabilizer states from Θ(n) samples.
Extend the framework to tolerant testing with quantum memory tradeoffs and to low-nullity states such as Clifford circuits with few T gates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal sample complexity results: Θ(n) copies for exact stabilizer learning, Θ(n-k+1/ε) for tolerant testing with k qubits of memory, and O(n2^r) measurements for stabilizer-nullity-r states.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on adaptive Clifford measurements and, for the tolerant-testing variant, may require limited quantum memory, so practical overhead and measurement-control fidelity could affect deployment.
paper_title: Adaptivity is all you need: Optimal stabilizer learning using just single-copy measurements
